# repometrics

Metrics for your code repository. A single function collates a wealth of
data from commit histories and GitHub interactions, converts it all to
standardised metrics, and displays the result as a single, interactive
dashboard of your repository.

## How?

### Installation

First, install the package either via
[`r-universe`](https://r-universe.dev):

``` r

options (repos = c (
    ropenscireviewtools = "https://ropensci-review-tools.r-universe.dev",
    CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"
))
install.packages ("repometrics")
```

or directly from GitHub with one of these two lines:

``` r

remotes::install_github ("ropensci-review-tools/repometrics")
pak::pkg_install ("ropensci-review-tools/repometrics")
```

The package may also be installed from locations other than GitHub, with
any of the following options:

``` r

remotes::install_git ("https://codeberg.org/ropensci-review-tools/repometrics")
remotes::install_git ("https://codefloe.com/ropensci-review-tools/repometrics")
```

### Use

The `repometrics` package has one main function for collating all data
for a repository:
[`repometrics_data()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_data.html).
This function has one main parameter, specifying the `path` to a local
directory containing an R package.

``` r

data <- repometrics_data (path)
```

A `repometrics` dashboard for the repository can then be launched by
passing those `data` to [the `repometrics_dashboard()`
function](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_dashboard.html):

``` r

repometrics_dashboard (data)
```

The dashboard will automatically open in your default browser.

## Prior Art

There are lots of tools for collating metrics of software repositories,
most of which are commercial and not open source. Notable open source
tools include those in the [github.com/chaoss
organization](https://github.com/chaoss), especially their
[augur](https://github.com/chaoss/augur) and
[grimoirelab](https://github.com/chaoss/grimoirelab) tools. Both of
these tools are huge and comprehensive. Although intended to be highly
configurable and customizable, they can be difficult both to set up and
to use. The [OpenSSF Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard) is a
lightweight system focussed on metrics of “security health”.

Plus a host of semi-private and commercial offerings like
[codescene](https://codescene.com/),
[SonarQube](https://www.sonarsource.com/),
[SonarGraph](https://www.hello2morrow.com/products/sonargraph),
[Teamscale](https://teamscale.com/), and
[Understand](https://scitools.com/).

project, you agree to abide by its terms.

# Package index

## Data collation

- [`repo_pkgstats_history()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repo_pkgstats_history.md)
  :

  Apply pkgstats across the git history of a package

- [`repometrics_data()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_data.md)
  : Collate 'repometrics' data for a local R package.

- [`repometrics_data_repo()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_data_repo.md)
  : Collate code and repository data for a local R package.

- [`repometrics_data_user()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_data_user.md)
  : Extract and combine data on all contributors to a repository.

## Dashboard

- [`repometrics_dashboard()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/repometrics_dashboard.md)
  : Start quarto dashboard with results of main repometrics_data_repo
  function.

## Auxiliary functions

- [`rm_metrics_list()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/repometrics/reference/rm_metrics_list.md)
  : List all implemented CHAOSS metrics
